subject: Islamic Studies
board: TGA Islamic Studies scheme (aqeedah, fiqh, seerah, hadith, akhlaq)
source: Adapted from TGA Drive RE/Islamic Studies folder (Al-Baseerah Salah quiz KS2: nafs, sincerity, praying on time, best deeds; Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies SOW, Theme 1 (life of the Prophet ﷺ) to shape the seerah sequence); National Curriculum RE (KS2)

lessons.title: The three categories of Tawheed
objectives: Define Tawheed ar-Rububiyyah, al-Uluhiyyah and al-Asma was-Sifat
Give a Qur'anic evidence for each
Explain why Uluhiyyah is the message of every prophet

keywords.def: Allah alone creates, owns and controls all things
believing in Allah's names and attributes as He described Himself

starter: Name three names of Allah with meanings.

teach.heading: Why divide Tawheed?
bullets: Scholars studied the Qur'an and Sunnah
They found three areas of Tawheed
It helps us understand and teach belief
teach.note: Bismillah. Explain that the three categories are an organised way to understand what the Qur'an teaches, as scholars of ahl as-sunnah have done. They are not separate beliefs; they work together. Draw a triangle on the board.

teach.heading: Rububiyyah: Lordship
bullets: Allah alone creates, owns and runs the universe
teach.note: 7:54: His is the creation and the command; blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds. Ask: what do you depend on that Allah controls? Even the idolaters of Makkah admitted Allah created the heavens and earth (29:61).

teach.heading: Uluhiyyah: worship
bullets: Prayer, dua, trust, sacrifice for Allah alone
This was the message of all prophets
teach.note: 51:56 and 16:36. The Makkans accepted Rububiyyah but still worshipped idols; therefore the Prophet ﷺ called them to Uluhiyyah. Ask: why is it not enough to say Allah is Creator? Because worship belongs to Him alone.

teach.heading: Asma was-Sifat
bullets: Allah has perfect names and attributes
42:11: nothing is like Him, He hears and sees
teach.note: Recap Year 4. Keep it to the method: affirm what Allah and His Messenger affirmed, without likening Him to creation, without denying, without asking how, without distorting meanings. Mention 20:5 as an example.

teach.heading: Put it together
bullets: Names lead to love and awe
teach.note: Give a quick example: knowing that Allah alone provides (Rububiyyah) means we only ask Him (Uluhiyyah), and knowing He hears (Names) means we make dua. Pairs complete a diagram.

practice: Why do we make dua to Allah only?
independent: Create a table: category / definition / evidence / example
Write a paragraph: why did Quraysh need to be called to Uluhiyyah?
Match statements to the category
exit: Name the three categories.
Which category was denied by the idol worshippers of Makkah in practice?
lessons.homework: Explain the three categories of Tawheed to a family member using one example each.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: three-column organiser with sentence frames. Stretch: explain why a Muslim cannot accept Rububiyyah without Uluhiyyah.

lessons.title: Tawheed in action: dua, trust and reliance
objectives: Explain that dua is worship
Explain tawakkul and its balance with effort
Explain why we direct worship only to Allah

keywords.def: calling on Allah in worship and need
relying on Allah while taking the means

starter: Name the three categories of Tawheed.
Who do we call on in dua?

teach.heading: Dua is worship
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said: dua is worship
Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud (an-Nu'man ibn Bashir)
Allah says: call upon Me, I will respond (40:60)
teach.note: Bismillah. Read the hadith and 40:60. Ask: why is dua called worship? Because it shows need and trust in Allah. Link to Uluhiyyah.

teach.heading: Ask Allah
bullets: If you seek help, seek help from Allah
teach.note: Read the hadith. Clarify: it is permissible to seek help from people in what they are able to do (e.g. a doctor). What is forbidden is asking creation for what only Allah can give. 27:62: He answers the distressed one.

teach.heading: Tawakkul
bullets: Trust Allah and take the means
5:23: rely on Allah if you are believers
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said to the man who left his camel untied and said he trusted Allah: tie it, then trust (Tirmidhi, hasan). Ask: what does this show? Tawakkul is not laziness.

teach.heading: Stories
bullets: Musa at the sea: My Lord is with me
teach.note: Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil was said by Ibrahim in the fire and by the Prophet ﷺ when told people had gathered against them (Bukhari, Ibn Abbas). Musa: 'Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me' (26:62). Link to tawakkul.

teach.heading: Our daily Tawheed
teach.note: Pairs write a list of everyday situations where they will ask Allah: exams, journeys, illness. Share. Encourage pupils to speak to Allah in their own words and to begin with Bismillah and end with Alhamdulillah.

practice: What do we say at the beginning?
independent: Write a dua for a difficult situation
Explain the camel hadith in your own words
Complete: Tawheed in action is when I ______
exit: Why is dua worship?
What is the balance in tawakkul?
lessons.homework: Make dua daily for a week for something important and keep a short log.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with sentence frames. Stretch: write a reflection on the balance of trust and effort.

lessons.title: Belief in Qadar: Allah's decree
objectives: Define Qadar and its four levels
Explain that humans have choice and responsibility
Explain how Qadar brings comfort

keywords.def: Allah's knowledge, writing, will and creation of all things

starter: Name the six pillars of iman.

teach.heading: The sixth pillar
bullets: Believe in Qadar, good and bad
teach.note: Bismillah. Recall the hadith of Jibril. Qur'an 54:49: indeed We created all things with qadar. Ask: why is it hard to understand? Remind that we accept what Allah told us.

teach.heading: Four levels
teach.note: Level 1, 'Ilm: Allah knows what was and will be (22:70). Level 2, Kitabah: everything is written. Level 3, Mashi'ah: nothing happens except by Allah's will (81:29). Level 4, Khalq: Allah created all things including our acts (37:96).

teach.heading: We choose
bullets: Allah gave us will and choice
teach.note: Qur'an 18:29: say the truth is from your Lord; whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve. Our choices are real, and are within Allah's knowledge and will. Do not use Qadar as an excuse for sin.

teach.heading: Effort and Qadar
teach.note: Muslim (Abu Hurairah): the strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak one, yet in both there is good. Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah's help and do not give up. If something befalls you do not say 'if only'; say 'Qadar Allah wa ma sha'a fa'al'.

teach.heading: Comfort
bullets: What missed you was not meant to hit you
teach.note: Know that what missed you was never going to befall you, and what befell you was never going to miss you (Tirmidhi, from the advice to Ibn Abbas). Ask: how can this reduce worry? Link to patience and gratitude.

practice: What does 'effort' have to do with faith?
independent: Explain the four levels in a table with an evidence for each
Write a reflection: how does Qadar reduce worry?
Answer: can we blame Qadar for sin? Explain.
exit: Name the four levels.
Give a verse about human choice.
lessons.homework: Discuss with family one hard event and how belief in Qadar helps; write a paragraph.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: four-level diagram with pictures. Stretch: write a short explanation of why choice and Qadar do not contradict.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Seerah: from Ta'if to the Hijrah
lessons.title: The Year of Sorrow and the journey to Ta'if
objectives: Describe the Year of Sorrow
Retell the Ta'if journey
Explain the Prophet's ﷺ mercy

teach.heading: Two great losses
bullets: It was called the Year of Sorrow
teach.note: Bismillah. In the tenth year of prophethood, within a short time. Abu Talib had protected him though he did not accept Islam. Khadijah was his comfort. Be sensitive. The Prophet ﷺ felt grief and continued to call to Allah.

teach.heading: To Ta'if
bullets: He went to Ta'if to seek support
teach.note: Seerah reports. The key authentic account is in Bukhari and Muslim (Aisha): she asked if any day was harder than Uhud; he said what he suffered at the day of Aqabah (Ta'if) from your people was hardest.

teach.heading: Angel of the mountains
bullets: An angel offered to crush the mountains
He hoped for believers from their descendants
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim: the angel of the mountains offered; the Prophet ﷺ said I hope Allah will bring from their descendants those who worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him. Ask: what does it show? Mercy.

teach.heading: Dua of Ta'if
teach.note: A famous dua is reported in the seerah; its chain is disputed, so teach the theme only: turning to Allah in weakness. Do not quote it as a hadith.

teach.heading: Lessons
bullets: Mercy to those who hurt us
teach.note: Discuss how to respond to unkindness. Link to the Qur'an: repel evil with what is better (41:34). Write a class lesson list.

independent: Write a short account of Ta'if using authentic details
Explain why the Prophet ﷺ refused the angel's offer
Role-play responding to unkindness with mercy
exit: Why is it called the Year of Sorrow?
What did he say about the people of Ta'if?
lessons.homework: Write a letter of thanks to someone who supported you in a hard time.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: timeline with key words. Stretch: link 41:34 to the story.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Seerah: from Ta'if to the Hijrah
lessons.title: Isra and Mi'raj: the gift of salah
objectives: Describe the Isra and Mi'raj using authentic sources
Explain how five prayers were prescribed
Explain lessons from the night journey

keywords.def: the night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem
the riding animal in authentic reports

starter: Why do we pray at set times?

teach.heading: The Qur'an speaks
bullets: Glory to Him who took His servant by night
From al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa
teach.note: Bismillah. Read 17:1. Note it came after the Year of Sorrow as a comfort and honour. Locate Makkah and Jerusalem on a map. Present only authentic details.

teach.heading: The ascension
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim describe meeting Adam, Idris, Musa, Isa, Ibrahim and others and reaching Sidrat al-Muntaha (Qur'an 53:13-18). Do not elaborate beyond the sources.

teach.heading: The gift of salah
bullets: Musa advised him to ask for reduction
Reduced to five with the reward of fifty
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim. The Prophet ﷺ returned several times until five remained; Allah said they are five and they are fifty. Ask: what does this show? Allah's mercy.

teach.heading: Reaction
teach.note: Reported in the seerah. Abu Bakr said if he said it, it is true. Link to belief in the unseen. Keep this as reported; the title as-Siddiq is well known.

teach.heading: Lessons
teach.note: Ask pupils: what should this gift make us feel? Gratitude. Revisit prayer on time.

practice: What happened in Year 10 of prophethood?
independent: Create a map of the Isra and Mi'raj route
Explain how 50 became 5 with the reward of 50
Write a paragraph: what does the gift of salah teach?
exit: What does 17:1 say?
How many prayers were prescribed in the end?
lessons.homework: Think about how you can improve your prayers this week and write three goals.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: map and sequence cards. Stretch: explain why the reduction shows mercy.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Seerah: from Ta'if to the Hijrah
lessons.title: The pledges of Aqabah and the Hijrah
objectives: Describe the pledges of Aqabah
Retell the Hijrah using authentic details
Explain what the Hijrah teaches

keywords.def: the place near Mina where the pledges took place

starter: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in the cave?

teach.heading: Pledges at Aqabah
bullets: Men from Yathrib met the Prophet ﷺ
They pledged to worship Allah alone
A second pledge to protect him
teach.note: Bismillah. Reported in the seerah: first a small group, then a larger pledge the next year. Mus'ab ibn Umayr was sent to teach them (reported). Present as reported.

teach.heading: Plan to leave
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ left with Abu Bakr
teach.note: Qur'an 8:30: when the disbelievers plotted against you, Allah planned; Allah is the best of planners. Ali's role is reported in the seerah. Be gentle in telling.

teach.heading: The cave
bullets: They hid in Thawr for three days
Do not grieve, Allah is with us
teach.note: Qur'an 9:40. Bukhari: Abu Bakr said if one of them looked down they would see us; the Prophet ﷺ said what do you think of two with Allah as their third? Asma bint Abi Bakr carried food (Bukhari).

teach.heading: Suraqah
bullets: Suraqah chased them for a reward
teach.note: Bukhari: Suraqah followed, his horse's legs sank in the ground; he asked for safety and was told to keep it secret. Present as in Bukhari.

teach.heading: Arrival
bullets: The people were full of joy
teach.note: The well-known poem 'Tala'al-badru' is widely quoted, but the report that it was sung at his arrival is weak; do not teach it as established. Say the people were joyful. Link to the community of Madinah.

practice: Where did the Prophet ﷺ hide?
independent: Write a newspaper report on the Hijrah
Explain three lessons from the Hijrah
Draw a route from Makkah to Madinah with key events
exit: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in the cave?
Who helped by bringing food?
lessons.homework: Research the route of the Hijrah and add one extra detail from an authentic source.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: route map and cards. Stretch: evaluate how trust in Allah appears in the story.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh: zakah, sawm and Hajj
lessons.title: Zakah: purifying wealth and helping others
objectives: Define zakah and its purpose
State the rate and the eight categories
Explain the difference between zakah and sadaqah

keywords.def: the minimum amount of wealth for zakah

teach.heading: Third pillar
bullets: It is joined with salah in the Qur'an
teach.note: Bismillah. Qur'an 2:43: establish prayer and give zakah. Many verses pair them. Explain zakah means purification and growth.

teach.heading: Who pays and how much?
bullets: Muslims who hold wealth above nisab
teach.note: The nisab is the value of 85 g gold or 595 g silver; check a trusted source for current amounts. Scholars agree on 2.5% for cash and gold. Children are not obligated; this is for understanding. Give a simple example: 2.5% of 1,000 is 25.

teach.heading: Who receives it?
teach.note: Qur'an 9:60 lists: the poor, the needy, collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, slaves, debtors, in the cause of Allah, travellers. Do not elaborate each in detail.

teach.heading: Zakah vs sadaqah
teach.note: Tirmidhi: smiling is charity. Also Bukhari and Muslim: every good deed is sadaqah. Ask for examples children can do.

teach.heading: Why zakah?
teach.note: Qur'an 9:103: take from their wealth a charity to purify and cleanse them. Ask: how does it build community? Link to the Ansar and Muhajirun.

independent: Calculate 2.5% of 2,000, 5,000 and 12,000
Write a paragraph on how zakah helps society
List five forms of sadaqah children can give
exit: What percentage is zakah?
Name one category who may receive zakah.
lessons.homework: Calculate 2.5% of a sample amount your teacher gives and present your reasoning.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: calculation steps with pictures. Stretch: explain why zakah is called purification.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh: zakah, sawm and Hajj
lessons.title: Sawm: fasting in Ramadan
objectives: Define sawm and its conditions
State what breaks the fast
Explain the exemptions and benefits

teach.heading: Obligation
bullets: So that you may attain taqwa
teach.note: Bismillah. Read 2:183. Ask: what is taqwa? Guarding oneself against wrongdoing with awareness of Allah. Ramadan is when the Qur'an was revealed (2:185).

teach.heading: How to fast
bullets: Abstain from food, drink and other things that break the fast
teach.note: Dawn to sunset (2:187). Explain fasting also means guarding the tongue and behaviour. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need of his leaving food and drink (Bukhari).

teach.heading: Excuses and mistakes
bullets: Forgetfully eating does not break the fast
teach.note: 2:185 for illness and travel. Bukhari and Muslim: whoever forgets and eats or drinks should complete his fast; Allah fed him. Children are not obliged to fast until puberty; encourage gradual practice.

teach.heading: Reward
bullets: Fast with faith and hope for reward
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever fasts Ramadan with faith and seeking reward, his previous sins are forgiven. Also: fasting has a gate called ar-Rayyan (Bukhari and Muslim). Ask: how do you feel about fasting?

teach.heading: Benefits
teach.note: Pairs list benefits of fasting. Share. Link to sabr and shukr.

independent: Create a Ramadan timetable for a day
Sort scenarios: breaks fast / does not break fast
Write a paragraph: how fasting builds taqwa
exit: Name two things that break the fast.
Who is exempt from fasting?
lessons.homework: Interview a family member about their experience of fasting and write three questions and answers.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with pictures. Stretch: explain why intention is needed.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh: zakah, sawm and Hajj
lessons.title: Hajj: the journey to the House of Allah
objectives: Define Hajj and Umrah
Describe the main rites at an introductory level
Explain the link to Ibrahim and Ismail

keywords.def: the sacred state with simple clothing
the plain where pilgrims stand on the 9th

teach.heading: A duty once in a lifetime
bullets: The Kaaba is the House of Allah
teach.note: Bismillah. Qur'an 3:97: pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by those who are able. The Prophet ﷺ said it is once; more is voluntary (Muslim). Ask: what does 'able' mean? Health and wealth.

teach.heading: Ibrahim and Ismail
bullets: They raised the foundations of the Kaaba
teach.note: Read 2:127 and the dua 'Our Lord, accept from us'. Link to Year 2 story of Ibrahim. Mention Ibrahim's call to pilgrimage (22:27).

teach.heading: The main rites
teach.note: Give a simple outline: Ihram (intention and clothing), Talbiyah ('Labbayka Allahumma labbayk'), Tawaf around the Kaaba, Sa'i between Safa and Marwa, standing at Arafah, Muzdalifah, Mina. Do not go into detailed fiqh differences.

teach.heading: Arafah
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said Hajj is Arafah (Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud). Ask: why is standing in dua so important? Link to dependence on Allah.

teach.heading: Reward
bullets: Hajj with no wrongdoing returns him sinless
Like the day his mother bore him
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever performs Hajj and does not commit obscenity or wrongdoing returns as the day his mother bore him. Compare Hajj and Umrah. Reflect.

independent: Draw a flowchart of the Hajj rites
Write a paragraph: why is Hajj a unifying experience?
Compare Hajj and Umrah in a table
exit: Name three rites of Hajj.
What does 'able' mean in 3:97?
lessons.homework: Research one rite of Hajj and prepare a one-minute explanation.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: step diagram with pictures. Stretch: link Hajj to the story of Ibrahim.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Hadith and akhlaq: advice, speech and truth online
lessons.title: The religion is sincere advice
objectives: State the hadith on naseehah
Explain how to give advice with adab
Explain how to accept advice

teach.heading: The hadith
bullets: For Allah, His Book, His Messenger
For the leaders and the common people
teach.note: Bismillah. Muslim (Tamim ad-Dari). Read and explain each: sincerity to Allah (worship), to the Book (reading and following), to the Prophet (obeying), to leaders and Muslims (wishing good).

teach.heading: Giving advice
teach.note: Ask: how would you like to be advised? The Prophet ﷺ was gentle (Qur'an 3:159). Model a gentle approach. Avoid embarrassing.

teach.heading: Receiving advice
teach.note: Role-play: a friend says you were rude. Respond with thanks. Ibrahim said to his father: gentle words (19:42-47) — keep it simple.

teach.heading: Not naseehah
teach.note: Distinguish between sincere advice and shaming. The Prophet ﷺ said a believer is the mirror of his brother (Abu Dawud, hasan). Ask: how is a mirror helpful?

teach.heading: Practice
teach.note: Pairs rewrite harsh messages into sincere advice. Share.

independent: Rewrite three harsh comments as sincere advice
Explain the hadith for each of the five groups
Create an advice guide
exit: What is naseehah?
Give two tips for giving advice.
lessons.homework: Give sincere advice to someone at home about something good and report how it went.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with starter sentences. Stretch: write a dialogue.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Hadith and akhlaq: advice, speech and truth online
lessons.title: Backbiting and gossip
objectives: Define backbiting (ghibah)
Explain the Qur'anic warning and the hadith
Give strategies to avoid it

keywords.def: backbiting: mentioning something about a person that they dislike
slander: saying something false about someone
return to Allah and put things right

teach.heading: The Qur'an
bullets: Would you eat the flesh of your dead brother?
teach.note: Bismillah. Read 49:12. Ask: why is the example so strong? It shows how ugly backbiting is. The verse continues: fear Allah; Allah is the Accepting of repentance.

teach.heading: The definition
bullets: Mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes
teach.note: Muslim (Abu Hurairah): the Companions asked, what if what I say is true? He said if it is true you have backbitten, and if it is not, you have slandered him. Discuss examples.

teach.heading: When is it allowed?
bullets: Asking a scholar for a ruling
teach.note: Scholars mention limited cases e.g. a wronged person complaining to someone who can help. Keep short: children should speak to a trusted adult about bullying. Link to safeguarding.

teach.heading: Stopping it
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever defends his brother's honour, Allah will shield his face from the Fire (Tirmidhi, hasan). Practise phrases.

teach.heading: Repair
teach.note: Ask: how can you repair? Make dua and apologise if the person knows. Role-play.

independent: Sort scenarios: backbiting / not backbiting
Write a polite way to leave a gossiping group
Explain 49:12 in your own words
exit: Define backbiting.
What should you do if you hear it?
lessons.homework: Spend a day avoiding gossip; reflect on any times you succeeded.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with images. Stretch: write advice to a friend who gossips.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Hadith and akhlaq: advice, speech and truth online
lessons.title: Adab online: truth, kindness and verification
objectives: Explain verification of news (49:6)
Explain the hadith about narrating all you hear
Apply adab to online learning and messaging

teach.heading: The verse
bullets: If a wicked person brings news, verify it
So you do not harm people unknowingly
teach.note: Bismillah. Read 49:6. Ask: how can false news cause harm? Examples from school messages, group chats. Emphasise verifying before sharing.

teach.heading: The hadith
bullets: It is enough lying to narrate all you hear
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it is enough lying for a man to narrate everything he hears. Discuss: forwarding messages, screenshots, posts. Link to amanah.

teach.heading: Kind communication
teach.note: Qur'an 49:11: do not mock; do not insult by nicknames. Teams chat rules in school. Review TGA online expectations. Report concerns to a trusted adult.

teach.heading: Privacy and protection
teach.note: Link to amanah and safeguarding. The Prophet ﷺ taught modesty and privacy. Do not require pupils to share personal examples.

teach.heading: My online code
teach.note: Pairs create a three-point code of adab online. Display.

independent: Check three claims: decide how to verify each
Write online adab rules for class chat
Rewrite unkind messages kindly
exit: Why verify news?
Name one rule for online adab.
lessons.homework: Show an adult your online code and discuss how to follow it.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards and sentence starters. Stretch: write a short guide for younger pupils.
